resumen: Feet very wide, toes out and a dumbbell hanging between the legs. The wider stance gets the adductors and glutes working harder.
ejecucion: Set your feet well wider than your shoulders, toes turned out.
Hold a dumbbell with both hands by one end, hanging between your legs with straight arms.
Squat down with an upright torso, pushing your knees out in line with your feet.
Go down as far as you can keep your back straight, without the dumbbell touching the floor.
Stand up by pushing the floor away.
matices: The study comparing stance widths in the squat found more gluteus maximus and adductor longus activity with a wider stance, and similar quadriceps. It used a barbell and moderate loads; with a dumbbell the principle is the same, but it has not been measured in the same way.
